key_insight: Two mathematical statements can be logically equivalent simply because both are provable—not because they express the same idea. SemantEq targets a more faithful, bidirectional notion of equivalence for evaluating AI-generated formal statements.
problem_solved: As automated provers improve, proving an AI-generated statement does not guarantee that it correctly translates the original mathematics. Ordinary logical equivalence against a trusted formalization can also accept statements with different meanings.
method: Use a trusted reference formalization to assess an automatically generated formal statement.
Target faithful correspondence in both directions, rather than accepting logical equivalence alone.
The supplied abstract is truncated, so the exact equivalence criterion and implementation are not available.
impact: More faithful statement evaluation could help practitioners detect translation errors that successful proof checking misses. This would improve confidence in AI-assisted formalization workflows such as Lean 4.
visual_elements: Translation pipeline: natural-language mathematics → AI-generated Lean statement → faithfulness check.
Two distinct, provable statements connected by a warning-labeled logical-equivalence symbol.
Bidirectional arrows between a trusted reference and a generated statement.
Separate indicators for proof correctness and translation faithfulness.
paper_title: SemantEq: Faithful Bidirectional Equivalence of Formal Statements
paper_authors: Xinrui Li, Pawan Sasanka Ammanamanchi, Siddharth Bhat, Rianna Jamdar, Yongxi Lin
